analysis.investment_thesis: PhysicsWallah is a loss-making edtech business trading at 433x EV/EBITDA with a D/E of 0.67 — failing every single financial quality test I apply. Three consecutive years of net losses, a balance sheet that went deeply negative (equity of -1,246 Cr in FY24), and explosive revenue growth funded by debt and equity dilution is exactly the kind of speculative story I stay far away from.
key_strengths: Strong revenue momentum — 131% CAGR from 233 Cr (2022) to 2,887 Cr (2025) shows genuine demand
Operating CF positive all 4 years including 507 Cr in FY25, suggesting cash-generative unit economics at the course level
High promoter holding at 72.3% signals founder commitment to the business
key_risks: Cumulative net losses of ~1,458 Cr over FY23-FY25 with no clear profitability timeline — net loss still -243 Cr in FY25 despite 2,887 Cr revenue
D/E of 0.67 far exceeds my hard limit of 0.3; borrowings ballooned to 2,461 Cr in FY24 before partial repayment
Extreme valuation — Forward P/E 99.68x and EV/EBITDA 433x prices in flawless execution for a decade in a business with zero proven earnings track record
red_flags: FY24 'Other Income' of -672 Cr is a massive red flag — almost certainly goodwill impairments or acquisition write-downs from the debt-funded expansion binge of 2023
Total equity was negative (-1,246 Cr) as recently as FY24; balance sheet only repaired via IPO proceeds — not from earned profits
ROE of -17.38% and ROCE of -2.12% — capital is being destroyed, not compounded
Aggressive investing outflows of -1,513 Cr in FY25 signals continued empire-building before the core business is proven profitable
analysis.detailed_analysis:
PhysicsWallah is built on explosive revenue growth — from 233 Cr in FY22 to 2,887 Cr in FY25 — but has burned through capital at every step. The business went from a 98 Cr profit in FY22 to cumulative losses of over 1,458 Cr in the three years that followed, wiping out all equity (negative 1,246 Cr in FY24) and requiring an IPO to recapitalize the balance sheet. The -672 Cr "Other Income" in FY24 almost certainly reflects goodwill write-downs from poorly priced acquisitions — a classic symptom of management overreach. D/E at 0.67 is simply not acceptable to me; I never invest in businesses where debt funds speculative growth.

The only faint positives are the high promoter stake (72.3%) and positive operating cash flows, including a decent 507 Cr OCF in FY25. But operating CF can flatter edtech businesses that collect fees upfront before delivering courses — it is not the same as durable free cash flow from a proven earnings engine. At 433x EV/EBITDA and 99.68x forward P/E, the market is pricing in flawless profitability for the next decade. I built DMart over 20 years by buying boring businesses at fair prices — PWL is the opposite of that: a glamour story at a glamour price with no earnings history to justify it. This is a pass for me.
